# TimeOfDay

A time within a day, to the nanosecond.

```rux
pub struct TimeOfDay {
    pub hour: uint8;
    pub minute: uint8;
    pub second: uint8;
    pub nanosecond: uint32;
}
```

`Copy`, and only constructible valid. The second stops at 59: leap seconds are a policy for the text boundary,
not a representable value here.

## Fields

| Name         | Type     | Description                   |
| ------------ | -------- | ----------------------------- |
| `hour`       | `uint8`  | The hour, 0 through 23.       |
| `minute`     | `uint8`  | The minute, 0 through 59.     |
| `second`     | `uint8`  | The second, 0 through 59.     |
| `nanosecond` | `uint32` | The fraction, in nanoseconds. |

## Implements Display

`TimeOfDay` conforms to `Display`.

<h3 id="write-display"><code>WriteDisplay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func WriteDisplay(self: &TimeOfDay, writer: &var TextWriter, spec: FormatSpec) -> ! FormatError
```

Writes the time as `HH:MM:SS`, with a fractional part when there is one.
A precision names exactly that many fractional digits, 0 through 9, and truncates. Without one the fraction
is written to the digits it has with trailing zeros trimmed, and omitted when it is zero.
Reports whatever the writer reported, `UnsupportedRequest` for a style other than `iso8601` or `rfc3339`,
and `UnsupportedRequest` for a precision past nine, which no fraction has.

| Name     | Type              | Description                    |
| -------- | ----------------- | ------------------------------ |
| `writer` | `&var TextWriter` | the destination                |
| `spec`   | `FormatSpec`      | what the placeholder asked for |

**Returns**: success when the whole time was accepted

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/Calendar.rux#L187)

## Related

<h3 id="parse-time-of-day"><code>ParseTimeOfDay</code></h3>

```rux
pub func ParseTimeOfDay(text: char8[..]) -> TimeOfDay ! TimeParseError
```

Reads `HH:MM:SS` with an optional fractional second.
Reports `InvalidSyntax` for a shape that does not match, `InvalidTime` for a field outside its range, and
`ExcessiveFraction` for more fraction digits than a nanosecond holds. Second 60 folds rather than failing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Time/Src/CalendarParse.rux#L246)

**Parameters**

| Name   | Type        | Description      |
| ------ | ----------- | ---------------- |
| `text` | `char8[..]` | the text to read |

**Returns**: the time of day, or why the text is not one
